I’ve always cared about staying healthy—nursing taught me that—but lately, things feel harder to manage. I lost my husband two years ago, and without him… meals just don’t feel necessary anymore. I used to cook for us both, but now I hardly eat. I’ve cut out bread, rice, anything starchy—I just can’t stomach the thought of it. Fats too. I know my body needs fuel, but the idea of gaining even a pound makes my chest tighten. I weigh myself every morning, sometimes more. If the number goes up, I’ll skip lunch or redo my stretches.  

There are times—more than I’d admit—when I eat a lot all at once, like a whole box of cookies, fast, without really tasting them. Afterward, I feel so ashamed I make myself vomit. It’s not something I plan, but the guilt is unbearable. I don’t know if I’m underweight—I haven’t had a proper check-up. The scale fluctuates, but I tell myself I’m just being careful. I just want control. But some days, I don’t recognize myself in the mirror.
D021-D022_h001.question_a:
I’ve always been mindful of my health, working as a nurse for over forty years, but lately, I find myself more and more focused on my weight. After my husband passed, I just didn’t feel like eating much, but now it’s become a constant battle. I’ve cut out almost all carbohydrates—no bread, pasta, rice—and I avoid anything with fat. I weigh myself multiple times a day, and if the number goes up even half a pound, I get so anxious I can barely breathe.  

Even though my daughter says I’m too thin—she’s begged me to eat—I feel like I still need to lose more. I’ve been underweight for months, according to my doctor, but I just can’t stop. There are times when I eat a bit too much—like when I have a sudden urge for sweets—and afterward, I feel so guilty I make myself vomit. It’s not that I’m eating all the time—I don’t—but when I do overeat, even slightly, I purge. But still, I keep trying to get even thinner. My clothes hang off me now, but in the mirror, I just see someone who needs to try harder.
D021-D022_h001.question_b:
I’ve been struggling for about three months now, and it’s gotten hard to ignore. Ever since my husband passed, I suppose I stopped taking care of myself the way I used to. As a nurse, I always prided myself on eating right, but now I find myself obsessed—avoiding carbs completely, cutting out fats, making sure everything is low-calorie. I weigh myself multiple times a day. If the number goes up even a little, I panic.  

But then… there are these episodes. I’ll be good all day, and by evening, I’m standing in front of the pantry, eating whatever I’ve hidden—cookies, bread, chips—until I can’t breathe. It feels out of control. Afterward, I’m filled with shame, so I make myself throw up. I’ve been doing it about once a week, sometimes more.  

My daughter says I don’t look thin, even told me I look fine, but I *feel* heavy. I know it doesn’t make sense, but I can’t stop. I’m not underweight—I’m actually around what the scale says is “normal”—but I just can’t accept it. The cycle keeps going, and I don’t know how to break it without feeling like I’m losing control completely.

    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D021-D022_h005.question_both: I’ve always been careful about what I eat, but lately it’s been harder to manage. I don’t eat much during the day—maybe a few bites at dinner, if that. High-calorie stuff, like pasta or anything with oil, scares me. I feel like just one bite will sit on me, show on my body right away. I record voiceovers from home, so I can schedule around my energy, but some days I’m so drained, my voice sounds weak, and clients notice. I’ve lost a little weight and honestly, I think I need to lose a bit more to feel in control. That said, sometimes I’ll eat a whole meal—more than I plan—especially late at night, and after, I just… get rid of it. Not all the time, but enough that I feel stuck. I don’t know if I’m eating *too little* or *too erratically*. I can’t tell if I’m underweight—my clothes fit loosely, but I don’t track numbers. It’s just that nothing ever feels like enough, and then right after, it feels like too much.
D021-D022_h005.question_a:
I’ve been trying to stay in control, especially with auditions coming up—my voice work depends on how I look, frankly. I’ve always been on the smaller side, but lately, I’m down to just a bite or two at meals, mostly plain rice or steamed vegetables. I can’t bring myself to eat more because the thought of gaining weight terrifies me—especially from anything “rich” like cheese or oil. Just a few bites feel safer.

There are times… I do lose control. Sometimes I eat a whole granola bar or a piece of toast with peanut butter, and after, I feel *huge*, like I’ve ballooned overnight. That panic drives me to throw up. It’s not frequent, maybe once or twice a week, but it happens. Still, I keep losing more weight—my ribs are so prominent now, and my clothes hang off me. My agent mentioned I look “fragile,” but I need to be lighter—just in case a role demands it.

I know I’m thin… maybe too thin, but I can’t stop. The scale needs to go lower. Safety means staying underweight. Control means resisting even the smallest extra bite.
D021-D022_h005.question_b:
I’ve been struggling for about three months now—maybe longer—and it’s starting to affect my work. I do voice acting, so I need to sound good, but honestly, I’m more focused on how I look. I get this intense fear around food, especially anything high in calories—like, I’ll see a muffin and immediately think, *That’s five pounds right there*. So I eat almost nothing during the day, sometimes just a few bites of salad or a piece of fruit.  

But then, around evening, I lose control. I’ll binge—fast food, sweets, anything I’ve denied myself—and I can’t stop. And afterward, I feel so guilty, so panicked about gaining weight, that I make myself vomit. I’ve been doing it at least once a week for months now.  

I know it’s not healthy, but I’m scared if I stop, I’ll get “fat.” The weird thing is, no one at work has commented on weight loss—actually, I was told I look “normal” at my last checkup. I’m not underweight. But I still feel like I need to lose more.

I’ve been on the road a lot—driving trucks for the past twenty years, alone most days. Honestly, I never paid much attention to eating. I just… don’t feel like I need much. I grab a coffee in the morning, maybe a protein bar if I’m hungry, but meals? They feel unnecessary. I’ve lost weight over the past several months—friends have noticed, even my ex-wife called me out on it. But I feel fine. A little lightheaded sometimes, especially after climbing down from the cab, and my hair’s been thinning. I just chalk it up to stress or aging.

There are times, though—long stretches on the highway late at night—when I’ll pull over and eat. A lot. Fast food, sweets, whole bags of chips. More than I should. And afterward… I feel so guilty, so out of control, that I make myself throw it up. I know it’s not great, but it’s the only way I feel like I can reset. I don’t do it every time, but often enough. I don’t know if it’s a problem, really. I’m just trying to manage. The scale keeps going down, but I don’t see the harm. I’ve always worked better lean.

I’m down to just over 120 pounds now, and I know I’m underweight, but every time I look in the mirror, I still see someone who needs to tighten up. I run a truck route most days, and the schedule’s tight, so I only allow myself a protein bar and black coffee—sometimes just water. 

Yeah, sometimes after holding back for days, I’ll eat an entire meal at a truck stop, maybe even two—bacon, eggs, pancakes—and then I panic. I make myself throw up or take laxatives. I know it’s dangerous, but I feel out of control when I eat too much. My hair’s thinning, and I’m always cold, even in the cab with the heater on. My ex-wife used to worry, but I tell her I’m fine. I just need to stay disciplined. The weight keeps dropping, but I figure that just means I’m doing something right.

But if I keep this up, I don’t know how much longer I can drive safely.  

It’s been going on like this, off and on, for about four months—more than once a week. I can’t quit, but I can’t keep living like this either.

I’ve always been careful about what I eat, but lately it’s gotten harder to manage. I run my own jewelry business from home, and with everything I’ve got on my plate—designs, deadlines, being a single mom sometimes—I don’t have much time or energy to think about meals. I try to keep it under 800 calories a day—just salads, tea, maybe a piece of fruit. Anything more and I start worrying, obsessing really, about putting on weight. I *hate* the idea of getting fat—it scares me more than I can explain.

My daughter says I look too thin, and my doctor brought it up last time, but they don’t get it. I’m not underweight—well, I don’t *think* so—and I exercise just enough to feel in control.  

But sometimes… sometimes I lose that control. Late at night, after a bad day or when a commission falls through, I’ll eat whatever’s in the house—crackers, chocolate, anything. And then I just feel so guilty, so panicked, that I make myself throw up. I know it’s not great, but it’s not like I do it all the time. Not enough to mean something’s really wrong, right?

For the past eight months, I limit myself to about 600 calories a day—nothing processed, mostly black coffee, greens, and plain chicken. I know people think I should eat more, but I can’t—not if I want to stay light. Gaining weight terrifies me. Even seeing a little fullness in the mirror sends me into a panic. My daughter and my doctor keep saying I’m too thin, that I need to gain weight, but I know my body better. They don’t understand that I’m not unhealthy—I’m disciplined.

Sometimes, yes, I do eat more—maybe a full meal or even dessert—and afterward, I feel so guilty, like I’ve ruined everything. So I make myself vomit or do extra hours on the elliptical. But even with those episodes, I’ve lost 35 pounds this year. My clothes hang off me now, but I still feel heavy. Honestly, I think if I let up even a little, I’d spiral out of control. I’m not underweight—I’m finally where I should be.
D021-D022_h025.question_b:
I’ve always been particular about my appearance—being a jewelry designer, I spend hours hunched over tiny pieces, and I like to feel precise, in control. But over the last few months, that need for control has taken over my eating. I restrict myself to barely 800 calories a day—salads, plain rice, black coffee—because I’m terrified of gaining weight. The thought of getting fat makes me anxious, almost panicky. My daughter keeps nagging me, says I look too thin, but I tell her she’s overreacting. I’m not underweight—I’m average, maybe a little lean, but not sickly.

The truth is, about twice a week, I lose control. I’ll buy a whole box of pastries or binge on frozen meals, eat it all in my studio late at night, hiding the wrappers. Afterward, I feel so guilty I make myself throw up. It’s been happening like clockwork for the past four months. I know it’s not healthy, but as long as I don’t gain weight, I tell myself I can handle it.
